title: Claim emits Claimed only when paid > 0; stake/unstake emits Claimed only when _safePay returned > 0 — inconsistent with rewardDebt advancement
description:
`stake` and `unstake` only emit `Claimed` when `_safePay`'s return value is non-zero, and `claim` only emits when `paid > 0`. Meanwhile, `rewardDebt` is advanced to the full `(amount * acc) / PREC` in all three paths regardless of whether anything was paid. That means a user whose pending was fully capped by `_safePay` (paid = 0) has their entitlement zeroed silently with no on-chain event — no `Claimed`, no `Unclaimed`, nothing. Off-chain indexers relying on events cannot detect the forfeiture.

Additionally, `claim()` uses a single local variable name `paid` while `stake()`/`unstake()` reassigns the outer `pending` variable to the return value of `_safePay` — the inconsistent naming masks the bug in CS-01 by making it harder to see that `user.rewardDebt` is computed from the original accrual not the paid amount.
impact: Silent forfeiture; off-chain accounting cannot reconstruct user debt from event logs.
proof: Read through lines 264-267 (stake), 290-293 (unstake), 313-317 (claim). In each, the Claimed event is gated on `paid > 0` but `user.rewardDebt` is assigned unconditionally on lines 278/296/315.
recommendation: Always emit a ClaimAttempted event with (entitlement, paid) so indexers can track shortfalls. Rename `pending` reassignment to a distinct `paid` variable for clarity. Tie this into CS-01's fix so the shortfall rolls over rather than being forfeited.
